prompt:
Image 1 is the club crest. Images 2 to 5 are photographs of this athlete.

A clean product photograph of a complete Basketball kit, laid out FLAT and neatly
arranged on a plain light grey surface, photographed from directly above.

EXACTLY ONE of each of these, in the frame, fully visible and not overlapping. A missing
item makes the plate unusable because the poses read the wardrobe from it — and a DUPLICATE
is just as bad, because two shirts leave the poses to choose which one is the kit:
- the shirt, laid flat and face up
- the shorts below it
- BOTH socks, laid out straight
- EXACTLY TWO SHOES IN THE WHOLE FRAME, never two pairs: ONE shoe seen from directly
  above, and the OTHER shoe of that same pair turned onto its side so its full profile
  and its outsole are visible. Two shoes, two views, so nothing about the footwear has
  to be guessed at when the poses are drawn from this plate.
- the ball or implement of Basketball

THE KIT — these are settled decisions, not suggestions. Do not substitute anything.
- shirt: Deep blue short-sleeved basketball jersey. Light blue piping around the V-neck collar and around both armholes, and a light blue panel running down each side from the armhole to the hem. FRONT: the club badge small on the wearer's LEFT chest, and the number 12 in light blue with a white outline centred on the chest below the neckline. BACK: the club badge SMALL and centred high on the upper back, clear of the number, and below it the number 12 large in light blue with a white outline. The badge never touches or overlaps the numerals. No club name, no sponsor and no lettering of any kind anywhere on it.
- shorts: Deep blue basketball shorts ending above the knee, with light blue trim along the hem and the club badge small on the wearer's LEFT leg. Plain otherwise, and no lettering.
- socks: Black crew socks, plain, with no logo.
- footwear: Dark blue and white high-top basketball sneakers with a white swoosh on the side — the same pair he wears in the photographs, shown clean. The same pair in every shot.
- equipment: A standard orange basketball with black seams, clean. The same ball in every shot.
- Where an item above is described from the athlete's own photographs, any manufacturer's
  logo it genuinely carries stays on it — that is their real clothing.
- The club crest goes small on the LEFT CHEST, about three fingers wide.

The photographs are attached only so you can SEE the items the list above
names. Do not take anything from them that the list does not name.

THE BADGE: take the artwork in image 1 and place it on the shirt UNCHANGED. Treat it as a finished graphic being applied to the garment, not as a subject to redraw or reinterpret: identical outline, identical figure inside, identical colours in identical places, identical proportions. Nothing added, nothing simplified, nothing restyled, and absolutely NO text — no club name, no letters, no word of any kind, not even small. POSITION: on the wearer's LEFT chest, which is the RIGHT side of the shirt as it lies facing you — level with the armpit, roughly a third of the way in from that edge. SIZE: about one twelfth of the shirt's width. It is the ONLY graphic in the entire set.

Hard requirements:
- Everything is BRAND NEW and immaculate: no dirt, no scuffs, no creases beyond the fold
  of laying flat, no wear, no sweat marks. Copy what they wear, never its condition.
- Flat lay from directly overhead. No mannequin, no person, no body, no hanger, no rail.
- Plain light grey surface, evenly lit, soft shadows only. No props, no background objects.
- BRANDING follows the list above, item by item: an item described from the athlete's own photographs keeps the manufacturer's mark it really carries, and an item that came from the sport default is plain and unbranded. Never ADD a swoosh, three stripes, a cat, a jumpman, a trefoil or a wordmark to something the list did not say has one — these marks carry no letters, so "no text" does not cover them and they have to be refused by name.
- No text of any kind, no numbers, no labels, no watermark.
- Sharp throughout, photographic, print quality. Square image.
